text:
maya (partnerships): Heads-up: OpenFrame (new model provider) submitted a contributor list but their license matrix is a bit messy. They included a CC-BY dataset and a few MIT components inside the training pipeline. We need to decide redistribution and attribution policy.

alex (product): For product, prefer allowing hosted API + Dedicated, but require that any redistribution outside Redwood (e.g., partner resellers, marketplaces) needs explicit permission. Also need benchmarks for quantized variants.

rachel (legal): CC-BY triggers attribution obligations. Redistribution is possible but attribution must be in the UI/metadata and in any downstream redistributions. We also need to confirm whether the dataset imposes ShareAlike (CC-BY-SA) or just CC-BY. If SA applies, that may force downstream artifacts to be under compatible license; thatould be a dealbreaker for marketplace redistribution.

openmodel-bot: SCAN_RESULT: detected CC-BY dataset mention in provided manifest; potential ShareAlike risk unknown. Recommend manual review.

maya (partnerships): OpenFrame claims CC-BY 4.0 for dataset A, and MIT for code. They provided a signed attestation but not GPG-signed commit hashes.

rachel (legal): Need: signed attestation + commit sigs or GPG-signed release + dataset provenance. Also ask provider to confirm whether they have cleared third-party contributions from contributors outside the declared list.

vincent (marketplace): If redistribution is limited, we can still list the model for consumption via hosted API and Dedicated. But the marketplace SKU must include flags: "attribution_required": true, "redistribution_allowed": false. We'll also add the exact attribution text to the listing.

alex (product): Suggest adding an opt-in telemetry agreement during canary to surface any customer takedown requests quickly. Also, limit initial traffic to small percentiles.

devops-bot: DEPLOY_CHECK: canary slot reserved on Dedicated pool d-canary-3. Auto-rollback hook available.

maya (partnerships): I'll request the commit signatures and clarification on CC-BY/CC-BY-SA. Also ask for a list of contributors with emails and contributor license assignments if any.

rachel (legal): I'll prepare a short memo on handling CC-BY models in the marketplace and template attribution language. Will include suggested user-facing copy like: "This model was trained in part on Dataset A (CC-BY 4.0); usage requires attribution: see [link]"

vincent (marketplace): If they can't provide commit sigs within 72h, we should refuse redistribution and only allow hosted access with limited promotion.

maya (partnerships): Action items: (1) Maya to ask OpenFrame for commit sigs, contributor CLAs, and CC-BY-SA confirmation (ETA 72h). (2) Rachel to draft marketplace memo + attribution template (ETA 48h). (3) Alex to prepare canary config and telemetry hook. (4) Vincent to prepare listing flags for non-redistributable models.

openmodel-bot: REMINDER: attach provider attestation to the marketplace ticket.

maya (partnerships): Scheduling a 20-min sync with legal & marketplace if they don't reply within 72h.

alex (product): If anything looks like ShareAlike, escalate to execs. That could affect revenue share with partners.

rachel (legal): Agreed. One more: check export-control matrix for contributors in embargoed countries.

maya (partnerships): Thanks all. I'll update the ticket and link docs here when received. :pray:
